chunks: Faḍālah narrated from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Do not place hanut in the ears of the deceased."

Because the correct understanding of the first narration, from his statement "in his mouth," is that it should be understood to mean upon his mouth, since it is not from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) that hanut be placed inside the mouth.

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the normative prophetic and Imamic practice
key_terms.الْحَنُوطُ: the funerary perfume applied to the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the dead person being prepared after death
key_terms.حَنُوطًا: camphor or perfumed substance used in funerary preparation
key_terms.فِي فَمِهِ: inside his mouth, as mentioned in the prior report
key_terms.مَسَامِعِ: the ears or auditory openings of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Should hanut be placed in the ears or mouth of the deceased in Islamic burial rites?
ai.summary: This hadith states that hanut should not be placed in the ears of the deceased. It also clarifies that an earlier wording about the mouth should be understood as applying to the outside of the mouth, not its interior, because placing hanut inside the mouth is not from the sunnah (prophetic tradition).
